\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جمنا} (jamnā)}{جمنا (jamnā)}]{\ur{جمنا} (jamnā) — to freeze; to set}

\label{lesson:UR-C372-jamna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to seep, then the Urdu for to split open.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جمنا}}
\textbf{\ur{جمنا}} — \emph{jamnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to freeze; to set\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{رات} \ur{کو} \ur{سردی} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{پانی} \ur{جم} \ur{جائے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar rāt ko sardī huī to pānī jam jāe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it is cold tonight, the water will freeze.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{دودھ} \ur{جم} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh dūdh jam gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جمنا}} (\emph{jamnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{jamnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to coagulate, to freeze\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{yamyátē}, \textquotedblleft{}is held fast\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10428).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jamnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jamnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar rāt ko sardī huī to pānī jam jāe gā.} — If it is cold tonight, the water will freeze.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to seep, then the Urdu for to split open, then say \emph{jamnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{جمنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To freeze; to set\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ابلنا} (ubalnā)}{ابلنا (ubalnā)}]{\ur{ابلنا} (ubalnā) — to come to the boil}

\label{lesson:UR-C372-ubalna-boil-up}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to split open, then the Urdu for to freeze.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ابلنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ابلنا}} — \emph{ubalnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to come to the boil\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{دودھ} \ur{ابلا} \ur{تو} \ur{وہ} \ur{گر} \ur{جائے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar dūdh ublā to voh gir jāe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the milk boils, it will spill over.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{پانی} \ur{ابل} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh pānī ubal gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ابلنا}} (\emph{ubalnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ubalnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to boil over\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*ubbal}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 2339); \textbf{\ur{ابالنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to boil (something)\textquotedblright{}, is its partner.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ubalnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar dūdh ublā to voh gir jāe gā.} — If the milk boils, it will spill over.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to split open, then the Urdu for to freeze, then say \emph{ubalnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گلنا} (galnā)}{گلنا (galnā)}]{\ur{گلنا} (galnā) — to soften in cooking; to melt away}

\label{lesson:UR-C372-galna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to freeze, then the Urdu for to come to the boil.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گلنا}}
\textbf{\ur{گلنا}} — \emph{galnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to soften in cooking; to melt away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{دال} \ur{نہیں} \ur{گلی} \ur{تو} \ur{اور} \ur{پکائیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar dāl nahīṅ galī to aur pakāiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the lentils have not softened, cook them longer.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{دال} \ur{گل} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh dāl gal gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گلنا}} (\emph{galnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{galnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to melt, to trickle\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{galati}, \textquotedblleft{}drips, oozes\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4074).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{galnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar dāl nahīṅ galī to aur pakāiye.} — If the lentils have not softened, cook them longer.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to freeze, then the Urdu for to come to the boil, then say \emph{galnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تڑکنا} (taṛaknā)}{تڑکنا (taṛaknā)}]{\ur{تڑکنا} (taṛaknā) — to crack (with a sharp sound)}

\label{lesson:UR-C372-tarakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to come to the boil, then the Urdu for to soften in cooking.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تڑکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{تڑکنا}} — \emph{taṛaknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to crack (with a sharp sound)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{گلاس} \ur{زیادہ} \ur{گرم} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{وہ} \ur{تڑک} \ur{جائے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar glās zyādā garm huā to voh taṛak jāe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the glass gets too hot, it will crack.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{شیشہ} \ur{تڑک} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh shīshā taṛak gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تڑکنا}} (\emph{taṛaknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{taṛaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be cracked\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{traṭ}, a crackling sound (CDIAL 5988).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṛaknā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṛaknā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar glās zyādā garm huā to voh taṛak jāe gā.} — If the glass gets too hot, it will crack.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to come to the boil, then the Urdu for to soften in cooking, then say \emph{taṛaknā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{تڑکنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To crack (with a sharp sound)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{درمیانہ} (darmiyānā)}{درمیانہ (darmiyānā)}]{\ur{درمیانہ} (darmiyānā) — medium; moderate}

\label{lesson:UR-C372-darmiyana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to soften in cooking, then the Urdu for to crack.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{درمیانہ}}
\textbf{\ur{درمیانہ}} — \emph{darmiyānā} — \textquotedblleft{}medium; moderate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آگ} \ur{درمیانی} \ur{رکھیں} \ur{گے} \ur{تو} \ur{کھانا} \ur{مزیدار} \ur{بنے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āg darmiyānī rakheṅ ge to khānā mazedār bane gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you keep the heat medium, the food will turn out tasty.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{درمیانہ}} (\emph{darmiyānā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{darmiyāna}, \textquotedblleft{}middle\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{darmiyān}, \textquotedblleft{}between\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darmiyānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darmiyānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āg darmiyānī rakheṅ ge to khānā mazedār bane gā.} — If you keep the heat medium, the food will turn out tasty.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to soften in cooking, then the Urdu for to crack, then say \emph{darmiyānā} again
\end{itemize}
